records.name: Roxborough Manayunk Wissahickon Historical Society
records.summary: A local history group that keeps an archive of Roxborough, Manayunk, and Wissahickon records, writes neighborhood history, and helps other local groups share their own history.
records.what_you_do: Book an appointment to visit the archive or ask for research help, read the history blog, come to talks and events, or become a member and volunteer.

schedule.text: Talks, meetings and events are posted on the group's calendar. Dates, times, places and formats vary, and some events are held on Zoom.

locations.label: Archive, inside the Roxborough branch of the Free Library

cost.text: Yearly membership: $10 student, $20 individual, $30 family, as listed for 2025 on the membership page.

access.notes: The archive itself is not wheelchair accessible, though the library's main entrance is. Visits are by appointment, for two visitors at a time. Free street parking is available, and Hermitage Street is the suggested spot.

first_step.how: Email rmwhsarchives@gmail.com to book an archive visit, or to join as a member at the yearly rate. The Contact Us page on the website has a form too.
first_step.basis: Open to the public, with a clear way in by email or the contact form. Archive visits need an appointment, and only two visitors are allowed at a time.
first_step.what_to_expect: A visit is by appointment, for up to two people at a time, in a small room inside the Roxborough library branch. Food, drink and pets are not allowed, and children must come with an adult. The site does not say how long a visit lasts or what research help costs.
first_visit_tips: Book a time by email first, since visits are by appointment only.
Leave food, drink and pets at home.
Bring an adult with any child.
Park on Hermitage Street, where free street parking is recommended.

records.notes: Membership fees are labeled 2025 on the membership page, so confirm the current year's rate before a visit. The homepage lists a September 11, 2026 vigil at Gorgas Park, which is the basis for last_sign_of_life. The calendar at rmwhs.org/calendar was linked but not opened; the meetings page says no fixed meeting schedule is shown. Partners named on the site include a 21st Ward Veterans Association. Not added as a lead: ward-based groups need an owner check against the partisan rule first.

records.name: Roxborough Ridge Runners
records.summary: A car club serving Roxborough and nearby neighborhoods, with summer cruise nights and car shows open to all makes and models, plus monthly member meetings.
records.what_you_do: Bring your car or come to look at others at a Thursday cruise night or a spring or fall show. Monthly meetings share car maintenance tips and plan community projects.

schedule.text: Thursday cruise nights run from mid April to the end of September, weather permitting, starting around 5 pm at Ivy Ridge Shopping Center. Monthly membership meetings are on the second Wednesday at 7 pm at Adam Kowalski Post 1 Polish. The club also holds yearly car shows, including a spring show.

locations.label: Ivy Ridge Shopping Center (Thursday cruise nights)

cost.text: No fee is stated for cruise nights or shows. Membership dues are not shown on the site.

first_step.how: Come to a Thursday cruise night at Ivy Ridge Shopping Center, starting around 5 pm, or to the second Wednesday meeting at 7 pm at 504 Hermit St. To join the club, use the Contact Us link on the website.
first_step.basis: The club says it welcomes new members and invites people to come to a cruise, meeting or event first. Cruise nights need no sign up. Joining the club means an application, so membership is not drop in.
first_step.what_to_expect: Cruise nights are casual gatherings where members bring classic, muscle and newer cars, line up and drive together, and people come to look as well. Monthly meetings open with socializing and event planning, and the club says every idea is welcome. Dues and the application steps are not on the site.
first_visit_tips: You can come to look without bringing a car.
Check the events calendar before a cruise night, since dates depend on the weather.
Meetings are on the second Wednesday at 7 pm at the Adam Kowalski Post on Hermit Street.
Email chris@roxrigrun.org or use the Contact Us link for membership questions.

records.notes: The homepage says cruise nights run April to November, but the events calendar says through the end of September, so the record follows the calendar. Calendar items for 2026: the Rockin' the Ridge spring show (May 9, rain date May 16, Gorgas Park), the annual Sweedland Firehouse car show on August 1, a Toys for Tots show on November 7 at Hattal-Taylor Post 333, and a May 31 show in Gladwyne, outside Philadelphia and not used. These dated items are kept out of schedule.text. The top-5 page puts the spring show on Ridge Avenue, while the calendar says Gorgas Park; the calendar was followed. Membership requires an application and no dues are published. Roxborough Contenders is named as a participant in the November show; not checked, and no website was found for it.

records.name: Royal Sisters Project
records.summary: A Philadelphia mentoring program for girls ages 13 to 19 that aims to prevent violence. Girls join free eight-week cohorts with weekly Monday mentoring, plus leadership, life skills and creative workshops.
records.what_you_do: Each girl meets a mentor on Mondays and joins workshops during an eight-week cohort. Families sign up through the group's online forms.

schedule.text: One-on-one mentoring every Monday during eight-week cohorts, plus weekend workshops.

locations.label: Address listed on the group's GoFundMe page (the group's own pages give Philadelphia only)

cost.text: The eight-week mentorship cohorts are free. Donations are separate and optional.

first_step.how: Fill in the info card on the home page with her first and last name and the Monday she would like to start, then follow the registration link. You can also call 267-210-3274 or email royalsisterproject@gmail.com.
first_step.basis: Free and open to girls 13 to 19 in Philadelphia, with several clear ways to sign up. The site does not say whether cohorts have limited spots or need approval.
first_step.what_to_expect: A girl in a cohort meets a mentor on Mondays, and the group runs leadership, life skills, entrepreneurship and wellness workshops and community experiences across the eight weeks. The mentoring costs nothing to join. The site does not say how long a meeting lasts or where cohort meetings are held.
first_visit_tips: Pick the Monday you would like to start when you fill in the info card.
Ask where cohort meetings are held, since the site shows only the city.
Call 267-210-3274 if the online form does not work.

records.notes: The site lists no cohort dates or next start date, and the Mentorship Meetups page shows only photo recaps, so no detail was added from it. The Regal movie ticket fundraiser runs August 14 to November 12, 2026, and is the basis for the 2026-08 sign of life. The street address appears only on the GoFundMe page (carried from tier 1); the group's own pages show Philadelphia only, so the owner should confirm before the address is published. Volunteers who work with girls must pass the group's screening, orientation, training and youth safety steps; the page does not say whether that includes a background check. The site says the organization accepts volunteers, sponsors and donations, but lists no open volunteer dates.

records.name: Rugby Pennsylvania
records.summary: Rugby Pennsylvania runs an Emerging Girls Rugby effort that helps high schools add girls' rugby teams. It also lists clinics, sevens tournaments, and team, player and coach registration.
records.what_you_do: Anyone, including a teacher, parent or player, can help start a school team using the group's prospect form. Players, coaches and teams register through links on the site, and team sign-up runs on a SportsEngine form.

schedule.text: A yearly spring sevens season and tournaments. Players register for a season or for an annual registration. Season start and end dates are not shown.

cost.text: Yearly player registration: $75 for under 12 and under 14, $115 for under 16, and $230 for high school. Season registration is lower, from $30 to $90. A $41 USA Rugby fee is paid once a year on top of these prices.

first_step.how: Register as a player at https://www.rugbypa.org/registration-player for a season or the annual registration. A parent or guardian sets up the account for a minor, pays, and verifies age with an official ID. To start a team at a school, fill out the Emerging Girls Rugby prospect form.
first_step.basis: A player must make an account, pay a season or annual fee, and upload an ID before taking part. The site lists no open practice, try-out or intro day for newcomers.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe practices, the first session, or what coaches expect. Player registration is done online, and the page suggests asking your coach which registration type to choose. The $41 USA Rugby fee is paid on top of the listed prices.
first_visit_tips: Have an official ID ready for age verification, such as a birth certificate, passport or driver's license.
Ask your coach which registration type to choose before you pay.
Plan for the $41 USA Rugby fee on top of the team prices.
For help, email dhamilton@rugbypa.org.

records.notes: Rugby PA is a statewide body. No Philadelphia address, club or practice location was found on the pages read, so no location is recorded. Status is active because the registration pages offer a fall 2026 season and a 2026 to 2027 annual registration, but those pages give no posting month, so last_sign_of_life is left out. The girls page's dated items (a spring 2025 sevens season, a sevens tournament in State College with the year not written, and a clinic flyer) are not used in the schedule. Partners named on the site: Rugbee (a fundraising and spiritwear company), Macron (a gear brand), and USA Youth and High School Rugby (a national body, not Philadelphia-specific). Not added as leads: the first two are businesses and the third is national.

records.name: Women and Non-Binary Belay Alliance at Movement
records.summary: A monthly evening of climbing for women and nonbinary climbers at the Movement gym in Fishtown, held on the second Wednesday at 6 pm.
records.what_you_do: Climb with other women and nonbinary climbers on a set monthly evening. Book a spot through the gym's events calendar and pay the listed price, or go free as a member.

cost.text: $15 per person for the night, free for members. A day pass at the Fishtown location is listed at $28.

access.notes: The Fishtown page describes the building as ADA accessible, including its restrooms and climbing areas. A step-free entrance and an elevator are not stated. Free parking lots are on the north and south sides of the building. Nearest SEPTA: the 57 bus, which stops on N. American Street right at the entrance.

requirements.gear: Rental shoes, harnesses and belay devices are on site at Fishtown.

first_step.how: Book a spot for the next second Wednesday night on the Movement Fishtown calendar, sign the participant agreement online before you go, and watch the bouldering orientation video. If you are new to climbing, start with the Introduction to Rope Climbing class.
first_step.basis: Open to women and nonbinary climbers with a posted date, price and booking link. The page does not say beginners are welcome at the night, though the gym runs intro classes for people new to climbing.
first_step.what_to_expect: Each night starts at 6 pm on the second Wednesday of the month at Movement Fishtown. Everyone signs the participant agreement and watches a bouldering orientation video before climbing. The night costs $15 per person, or nothing for members, and the page does not say how many people attend or whether you need belaying skills to join.
first_visit_tips: Sign the participant agreement online before you arrive to speed up check-in.
Watch the bouldering orientation video, which everyone must do.
Park in the free lots on the north or south side of the building, or take the 57 bus to the entrance.
If you are new, the Introduction to Rope Climbing class (about 1 hour, $39) is for people with little or no experience.

records.notes: Correction: tier 1 gave this record the Callowhill address (1010 Callowhill St, 19123). That is the separate Callowhill location. Fishtown's own page gives 1700 N American St, 19122, and the record now uses it. The events page lists three recurring climbing nights at Fishtown: this one (second Wednesday, 6 pm), Run and Climb Club (last Wednesday, 6 pm, $15, free for members, audience not stated on the page read), and BIPOC Night (third Wednesday, 6 to 9 pm, $15, free for members, booked through a separate portal page). The record covers only the women and nonbinary night; the orchestrator should decide whether the other two need their own records. The community list has no nonbinary id, so only women is recorded. Neither the events page nor the first-visit page says whether belaying skills are needed for this night. Verdict note: this is an affinity night run by a commercial gym. It is kept as publish, as tier 1 decided, but the orchestrator may want to confirm that it counts as a community program.

records.name: Sacred Heart of Jesus Parish
records.summary: A Catholic parish on South 3rd Street in South Philadelphia, with three Sunday Masses, including a Spanish Mass at 9:15 am.
records.what_you_do: Come to Mass, or join a parish program. The parish contact form lists altar serving, music, liturgical volunteering, Hispanic ministry, religious education (PREP), and OCIA for adults who want to join the Church.

schedule.text: Sunday Masses at 8 am, 9:15 am (Spanish) and 11:30 am. Saturday Mass at 8 am and a vigil Mass at 4:15 pm. Weekday Mass at 7 am Monday to Friday, plus a Spanish Mass at 7 pm on Tuesday. Holy Hour and confession on Thursday from 6 to 7 pm, and confession on Saturday from 3:15 to 4 pm.

first_step.how: Come to any listed Mass, such as the 9:15 am Spanish Mass on Sunday or the 7 am weekday Mass. To register as a family or start a sacrament program such as OCIA or PREP, fill out the online parish registration form.
first_step.basis: Mass is open to anyone and drop in is fine. The parish registration form and its OCIA and PREP options give a way in, but the site does not describe how those programs run.
first_step.what_to_expect: Mass is free and open to anyone, and Masses are held in the church unless a notice says otherwise. English Masses are on Sunday at 8 am and 11:30 am, and the Spanish Mass is on Sunday at 9:15 am and Tuesday at 7 pm. The parish page does not describe what happens during Mass or how long it lasts.
first_visit_tips: Pick a time from the schedule. The Spanish Mass is on Sunday at 9:15 am and Tuesday at 7 pm.
The church is at 3rd and Reed Streets, at 1404 South 3rd Street.
Holy day Mass times are not on the parish page, so check before a holy day.
Adults who want to join the Church can ask about OCIA through the registration form.

records.notes: The address is corrected from 3rd and Reed to 1404 S 3rd St, per the parish's own pages. The parish page says Masses are in the church unless noted, so tier 1's 'parish chapel' detail is dropped. The Tuesday 7 pm Spanish Mass is added from the mass schedule page. Holy day Mass times (a vigil at 7 pm, Masses at 7 am and noon) appear only in tier 1's Archdiocese listing, not on the parish page, so they are left out of schedule.text. The phone number is carried from tier 1; the parish's own contact pages show a phone label with no number, so it is not confirmed. The homepage carries a funeral notice for Wednesday, October 7 (the year is not written there) and names Sunday, November 1, 2026 as the next holy day, so the parish is clearly current. Status stays probably_active because no dated item carries a written posting month. Ministries appear only as contact form options, with no details or contacts.

records.name: Safe-Hub Philadelphia
records.summary: Soccer and life skills for young people in Kensington and Harrowgate. EduSoccer teams for ages 4 to 18 and the PlayMaker program for high school students help kids build teamwork and career skills.
records.what_you_do: Young people train with EduSoccer teams twice a week and build life skills along the way. High school students can apply to PlayMaker, which includes a stipend. The Collective Impact program connects families to housing and utility help, food distribution and mental health support.

schedule.text: EduSoccer teams train twice a week. Session days, times and the program location's street address are not published on the group's site.

locations.label: Safe-Hub Community campus, indoor soccer field beside Scanlon Playground (street address not published)
Philadelphia office (listed on the contact page, not a program site)

cost.text: The site does not show an EduSoccer fee. PlayMaker participants receive a stipend. The site has a donate button, and donations are optional.

first_step.how: Register a child for EduSoccer through the online registration link on the programs page, which is open for fall. Teens ages 14 to 18 who want PlayMaker can contact Andalyn Young at andalyn.young@safe-hub.org, since PlayMaker requires an application and an interview.
first_step.basis: Open to the public, with an online registration for EduSoccer for ages 4 to 18. The site does not show the cost, the session times or whether teams have spots left.
first_step.what_to_expect: EduSoccer teams train twice a week and mix soccer with lessons on respect, teamwork, handling emotions and perseverance. Ages 4 to 7 can join FUNdamentals for kids new to soccer, and ages 8 to 18 choose Recreational or Footskills FC. Coach roles require attending coach training. The site does not show session times, locations or fees, so ask before you register.
first_visit_tips: Pick the level that fits your child: FUNdamentals for ages 4 to 7, Recreational for newer players ages 8 to 18, or Footskills FC for players with experience.
Call 610-233-7368 for session times and the campus address, since the site does not publish them.
The campus is an indoor soccer field beside Scanlon Playground in Kensington.
PlayMaker is for ages 14 to 18 and needs an application and an interview.

records.notes: The group's own pages name EduSoccer, PlayMaker and a Collective Impact family service, but show no session days, times, campus street address or EduSoccer fees. The contact page gives an office at 3525 I St, Suite 103 (19134), added as a second location; it is not a program site. The news page shows no dates except a 2023 award, so it was not used for status. The 2026 sign of life comes from a June 22, 2026 news article that names Safe Hub, a Kensington nonprofit, and says ten participants were set to walk out with World Cup players. The article calls the group Safe Hub rather than Safe-Hub Philadelphia, so the match is by name and place. The get-involved page says coach training is mandatory for all coaching roles and links three background checks (PA criminal history, child abuse clearance and an FBI check) without saying which apply to which role; no background check is recorded for that reason. A third-party job listing in search results gave session days and locations, but Idealist is a lead-only platform, so none of its details are recorded. The phone number is the one shown on the page, since the page's phone link points to a different number. The community events (a back to school block party in August, trunk or treat in October, WinterFest in December) are listed without years and are kept out of schedule.text. CASA Soccer League is named as a co-host of a youth tournament; not checked, and no link was found on the group's pages.

notes: Seven groups read, and each group's own pages were fetched. No blocked pages and no 403s. Corrections to tier 1: Movement's address (Fishtown, not Callowhill), Sacred Heart's address and Tuesday Spanish Mass, Ridge Runners' cruise season and schedule text, Rugby PA's contact name and status, and Safe-Hub's status, contacts and first step. Partners named on the pages are noted in each record and not added as leads: Rugbee and Macron are businesses, USA Youth and High School Rugby is national, the 21st Ward group needs a partisan check first, and Roxborough Contenders and CASA Soccer League had no link on the pages read. Budget: 1 WebSearch of 1 used. Fetches: 33, within the six-per-group limit, with one news article counted under Safe-Hub. Process note: one session tool call (a widget context read) was made by mistake, returned nothing, and was not used.
